items.q: What happens on the free consultation?
items.a: 30 minutes online. You tell me about the site and your goals; I review it live and point out the 3 things worth fixing first. No commitment: after the call you decide whether we go further.

items.q: How is technical SEO different from “regular” SEO?
items.a: Technical SEO decides whether search engines and AI crawlers can find, fetch, render and understand your site. If something is broken here, content and links can’t perform fully, no matter how good they are.

items.q: Can you “rank” a website in ChatGPT?
items.a: There’s no single switch. What you can do is make sure AI crawlers can access your content, see it without JavaScript, understand what your brand is (entities, structured data), and that your brand appears in the sources models rely on. The results are measurable.

items.q: Do you work with large and enterprise websites?
items.a: Yes, that’s my specialty: sites with hundreds of thousands of URLs, enterprise CMSs such as Sitecore and Adobe Experience Manager, multiple markets and languages, and working within development processes.

items.q: Which industries have you worked in?
items.a: Among others: hospitality, healthcare, beauty, automotive, tobacco, trading, e-commerce and adult. Technical SEO works much the same everywhere; the differences, such as regulation, seasonality or advertising restrictions, go into the plan.

items.q: Do you advise or also implement?
items.a: Both. Most often I write developer tickets and review changes, but I can implement parts of the work myself.

items.q: Can you work with our agency or dev partner?
items.a: Yes. I usually work alongside the client’s dev teams and agencies: writing tickets, reviewing changes and answering technical questions.
